{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2022}} {{Use Philippine English|date=December 2022}} [[File:Camarines_Sur_Congressional_Districts.svg|thumb|300x300px|Camarines Sur divided into five districts]] {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Camarines Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Camarines Sur]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|independent city]] of [[Naga, Camarines Sur|Naga]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province and the city are currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through their [[Camarines Sur's 1st congressional district|first]], [[Camarines Sur's 2nd congressional district|second]], [[Camarines Sur's 3rd congressional district|third]], [[Camarines Sur's 4th congressional district|fourth]], and [[Camarines Sur's 5th congressional district|fifth]] congressional districts. == History == [[Camarines Sur]] was represented as part of [[Ambos Camarines]] until it was granted its own representations in 1919. It was divided into two [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|legislative districts]] until 1972. It was part of the representation of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa|Region V]] from 1978 to 1984, and from 1984 to 1986, it elected 4 assemblymen at-large. In 1986, it was redistricted into four [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|legislative districts]]. The passage of Republic Act 9716{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_14/RA09716.pdf |title=Archived copy |website=www.congress.gov.ph |access-date=January 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223004/http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_14/RA09716.pdf |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead}} created an additional district out of towns from the first and second districts, which elected its first representative starting in the 2010 elections. As a result, the numerical designations of the province's districts were also changed in order to accommodate the new district. Then-[[Senate of the Philippines|Senator]] [[Noynoy Aquino]] challenged the controversial law in court, arguing its alleged unconstitutionality because the reapportionment creates a district that does not meet the 250,000 population requirement outlined in the Constitution.[https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/story/175711/noynoy-asks-sc-to-strike-down-law-on-new-camsur-district Noynoy asks SC to strike down law on new CamSur district] However, the Supreme Court deemed that the creation of a district not meeting the 250,000 population requirement in the constitution is a rule only applicable to cities, not provinces, and therefore ruled that the district is constitutional.[http://www.thepoc.net/breaking-news/local/5745-sc-affirms-new-camsur-district.html SC affirms new CamSur district] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620230810/http://thepoc.net/breaking-news/local/5745-sc-affirms-new-camsur-district.html|date=June 20, 2010}} == Current districts == '''Political parties''' {{columns-list|colwidth=10em| {{legend|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|[[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] (3)|border=1px solid #aaaaaa}} {{legend|{{party color|Nationalist People's Coalition}}|[[Nationalist People's Coalition|NPC]] (2)|border=1px solid #aaaaaa}} }} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Camarines Sur]] !District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative !Party !Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] !Population (2020) !Area !Map |- ![[Camarines Sur's 1st congressional district|1st]] | style="background:{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}};" | |{{CSS image crop|Image=Rep.
